# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS

## BOOK 1: "Pride and His Prisoners" by A. L. O. E. (Gutenberg 60149)

**Frame/Preface (Ch. I–III):** Narrator personifies Pride and Intemperance as spirits on Nettleby Tower's battlements, Somersetshire, spring Sabbath morning. Tower: Norman robber-hold, moat dry, portcullis rusted, siege marks from Commonwealth; long lawsuit owner Mr. Auger (holds property); tower "haunted" by evil spirits. Last Mr. Bardon disinherited only son Timon for marrying a farmer's daughter. Pride boasts of influence over Hugh Bardon (father), through pride of ancestry; Intemperance boasts gin-palaces. Pride: "acid fermentation," "vinous," third stage. Pride says he has one foe: Spirit of the Gospel (David/Goliath). Pride's arts: "pardonable weakness," "natural instinct," "generous virtue." Points at pastor's daughter Ida Aumerle (soft dark eye, Ithuriel's spear). Ch.II history of Ida: mother died when Ida 12; sister Mabel (younger, impulsive, fearless). Ida's conversion at ~night in her room, lamp, reading Bible; "birthday of a soul." Ida declined Earl of Dashleigh (Reginald) proposal at uncle Augustine Aumerle's home, Aspendale; Dashleigh then married cousin Annabella. Ida's father Lawrence Aumerle (vicar of Ayrley) remarried Miss Lambert (Mrs. Aumerle, practical, "common sense," "Barbara Aumerle"). Pride fosters Ida's resentment of step-mother. Ch.III: Mrs. Aumerle condemned Ida's anthem trio; Ida gave up music charge. Lawrence's first wife died; her death humbled him. Augustine Aumerle: brilliant, handsome, sceptic (reason over revelation). Timon Bardon (white hair, "old lion") passes. Narrator's moral: reader ask if a prisoner of Pride.

**Ch. IV – Cottage (Mill Cottage / "Milton Cottage"):** Stone cottage, two storeys, iron knocker, verandah apology, polyanthus garden. Cecilia Bardon (30s–40, sallow, light tresses, grey eyes), vanity about dress; fawn-coloured kid boots; no fire April 1–November; pink paper cards of Countess's wedding (Annabella married ~1 year 10 months earlier). Dr. Timon Bardon, surgeon, poor practice; "It's the fool that gets on in the world." Ida and Mabel bring crimson curtain. Annabella's invitation to Dashleigh Hall via Ida. Doctor's hyacinths gift. Mabel's "mental glass" joke (magnifier/diminisher).

**Ch. V – Both Sides:** Mabel calls Mrs. Aumerle "crockery" vs "porcelain." Ida plans farm-boys' class Saturday evening; conflicts with mothers' meeting; Mrs. Aumerle's scolding about walking after sunset. Mrs. Aumerle insists Ida not teach; Pride whispers. Mrs. Aumerle quotes James 4 "God resisteth the proud." Mrs. Aumerle proposes she herself takes the lads.

**Ch. VI – Visit to the Hall:** Cecilia persuades father; donkey-chaise from farmer neighbour (Pelton 6 miles off). Cecilia's dress and dusty boots. Lodge-keeper Mills. Doctor: "Mere gingerbread!" of Hall. Annabella (Titania-like, small, vivacious dark eyes, ink stain, writing romance) greets them warmly; wins doctor over by asking for a slip of his Venice Sumach.

**Ch. VII – A Misadventure:** Annabella's backstory: orphan, grandmother's pet; pen-name "Egeria." Earl Reginald proposed out of pique. Marriage sour; Pride whispers to each. Earl's pride; Duke of Montleroy invited to luncheon. Donkey brays, startles earl's horse; earl thrown. Earl orders "Tell Mills…" Butler: covers laid for four. Annabella keeps guests waiting; earl rings. Doctor overhears "Can't you manage some way of getting rid of these miserable Bardons?" Doctor's outburst: "gilded puppet," "never enter my presence." Pride triumphs.

**Ch. VIII – A Brother's Effort:** Vicar Lawrence in study with Augustine (German philosophy). Debate on reason vs faith; Ps. 131; "natural man receiveth not"; sin/spiritual pride; Augustine: "Lay aside the Scriptures." Augustine asks about origin of sin. Augustine leaves; Lawrence prays on knees.

**Ch. IX – Disappointment:** Annabella's romance proofs "Egeria"; earl forbids publishing for hire ("Countess to work for hire!"); offers private circulation; Annabella: "Tyrant!" (Pride whispers). She writes satire "The Precipice and the Peer" (Swiss mountain, earl's giddiness, lady's boa).

**Ch. X – On the Watch:** Ida and Mabel in arbour. Ida: works broken ladder rounds; prayers; "dearest idol" hymn. Pride stays aloof.

**Ch. XI – The Quarrel:** Balloon ascent from Augustine's grounds (Aspendale) with aeronaut Verdon, balloon *Eaglet*. Earl finds "The Precipice and the Peer" in drawer, tears it, tramples. Earl: "Leave the room, insolent girl!" Duke of Montleroy witnesses. Annabella orders carriage, goes to vicarage.

**Ch. XII – The Unexpected Guest:** Storm evening at vicarage; Doctor and Cecilia present; Cecilia sings "Bel raggio lusinghier." Mabel asks to fly with uncle; Mrs. Aumerle: "That's pride." Doctor refuses to meet earl. Annabella arrives haggard; Lawrence takes her to study; Ida to share Mabel's room.

**Ch. XIII – The Friend's Mission:** Mrs. Aumerle vs Mabel. Augustine's mission to earl: earl will pardon if Annabella apologises. Annabella refuses; calls for Dr. Bardon.

**Ch. XIV – A Fatal Step:** Bardon tells Annabella false rumour (Papists, mass, prayer to Virgin); urges her to publish satire to revenge. She sends two envelopes (magazine & publisher letter putting "Countess of Dashleigh" name on "The Fairy Lake"). Ida tries to see her, refused. Mabel offers to recall Bates; Annabella says "No." Bates posts letters.

**Ch. XV – The Deserted Home:** Earl's remorse; reads Magazine ad "The Fairy Lake" and satire. Lawrence's letter. Earl writes Augustine to reserve balloon place.

**Ch. XVI – Pleading:** Ida pleads; Mrs. Aumerle rebukes Annabella; Annabella leaves for Dr. Bardon's cottage. Ida regrets not going earlier.

**Ch. XVII – Conscience Asleep:** Bardon buys Magazine at Pelton library; Mrs. Clayton (blind widow); reads satire with glee. Bardon hears Auger died (of Nettleby Tower). Annabella moves into Mill Cottage. Cecilia gives up her muslin for her room.

**Ch. XVIII – The Magazine:** Bardon's cruelty; Cecilia sews drugget.

**Ch. XIX – Expectation:** Earl to ascend in *Eaglet*. Mabel gets father's permission, not mother's consent. Mrs. Aumerle refuses; vicar: "I daresay you were right."

**Ch. XX – A Sunny Morn:** Mabel to Aspendale early (12 May). Augustine, Verdon. Earl arrives pale.

**Ch. XXI – The Ascent:** Earl panics, lunges; cry "Let go!" The balloon released; Verdon: "They are lost!"

**Ch. XXII – In the Clouds:** Augustine pulls valve rope, snapped; gas not vented; whirlwind; earl faints.

**Ch. XXIII – Regrets:** Ida's guilt; Ida tells Annabella's Bardon news; Bardon brings news; Annabella curses Bardon.

**Ch. XXIV – Soaring above Pride:** Night in balloon; earl's text "loftiness of man shall be bowed down"; Mabel writes note to Mrs. Aumerle, drops it; earl drops pocketbook (Annabella's gift with two words written). Prayer, Litany.

**Ch. XXV – A Broken Chain:** Annabella grief; Ida's confession to Mrs. Aumerle; Mrs. Aumerle embraces her.

**Ch. XXVI – The Awful Crisis:** Augustine's reflections; balloon sinking into Channel; ballast/instruments thrown; car cut loose; rescue by sailing fishing vessel (smack).

**Ch. XXVII – Tidings:** Annabella sends cancellation of her romance. Telegram from Augustine: "Safe, thank God!" earl brain fever at Cliff Cottage, Devon. Mrs. Aumerle sends Ida. Mabel's letter found.

**Ch. XXVIII – The Wheel Turns:** Bardon inherits Nettleby Tower (Auger's will; reimburses lawsuit costs). Annabella goes to Devon at night; fisherman's cottage on shore.

**Ch. XXIX – Two Words:** Dr. G—— bars Annabella from sickroom. Augustine & Lawrence conversation: "Tribulation worketh patience." Earl recovers; pocketbook pencilled "forgiveness" and "peace." Annabella reconciled.

**Ch. XXX – The Spirit Laid:** July; earl and Annabella reconciled, proposal to call on Bardon; Bardon at Nettleby Tower, earl offers handshake; enmity ends. Closing essay on pride (poem "Proud,—and of what?").

---

## BOOK 2: "Feathers Left Around" by Carolyn Wells (Gutenberg 75642, 1923)

**Setting:** Valhalla, Valentine Loft's estate, Westchester County. Loft (32, lawyer/architect/financier, "Do nothing and all will be done" maxim, hates divorce). Fiancée Pauline Fuller (tall, dark, black eyebrows, aunt in NYC, chaperone Anna). Guests: Ned Knox (writer of detective stories, undersized, jealous husband) and wife Anna Knox ("Little Anna," blonde, flirt, separate bedrooms with bath between); Angel Bob Baldwin (Viking, blue eyes, book dealer, "Baldwin and Co."); Countess Galaski (Russian, rouged, blunt); Stella Lawrence (ash-blonde, psychic, trailing draperies); Jack and Mrs. Meredith (Mr. Meredith dreams of woman in shawl); Roly Mears (young, incorrigible, amateur detective). Servants: Binns (butler), Mrs. Jennings (housekeeper), Bates (Anna's/Pauline's maid), Tessie (chambermaid), Violet (parlour maid), Gideon (night watchman), Mills? (no). Dr. Gilvray (County Medical Examiner); Detective Kinney; Jackson (investigator); Miss Hetty Dwyer (Curran's sister, tall, gaunt, black taffeta, quill hat).

**Victim:** Hugh Curran (real name Hugh Dwyer), detective-story author, ex-movie actor, divorced, from Indiana, book collector.

**Key events:**
- Ch I: Valhalla party; Anna names house; discussion of murder methods (strangling, shooting, stabbing, poison). Curran invited (book-collector).
- Ch II: Curran arrives; "feathers left around" anecdote (chicken thief). Curran walks with Anna and Angel; asks Anna about divorce.
- Ch III: Dinner; Curran's mind-reading ("Rosalie," "Mr. S."); Pauline's reaction. Curran found dead in locked room, chair, hydrocyanic acid; Loft & Binns break door. Curran had asked Angel for Caxton book; Angel left ~12:40.
- Ch IV: Doctor Gilvray: Prussic acid, no container. Meredith saw woman in shawl enter Curran's room; Curran's door closed again ~2:30.
- Ch V: Roly leads amateur squad; watch missing; Curran's book catalogue; Angel's needle quarrel; Countess suspects.
- Ch VI: Ned suspects Angel (needle); Tessie saw Anna & Curran on balcony at 1 a.m.; Violet/Tessie statements; Kinney.
- Ch VII: Loft suspects Ned; Miss Dwyer arrives; reveals brother's divorce from "Rosalie" (married ~8 months, divorced ~6 yrs ago).
- Ch VIII: Kinney seduced by Anna (balcony alibi; tap at door; visitor a woman). Miss Dwyer's motive theory (rare books). Stella's dream ("Rosalie," "Mr. S.").
- Ch IX: Countess tips Kinney to search rooms. Kinney finds Curran's watch hidden in Pauline's locked desk, picture of Pauline. Pauline sobbing "I must forget."
- Ch X: Loft denies; Loft tells Kinney Pauline left (Pauline gone).
- Ch XI: Pauline flees on 4:45 train (Tessie packed bag); "Good-by" message. Loft predicts she left at a way-station for Boston/Albany. Kinney suspects Pauline; Miss Dwyer suspects her.
- Ch XII: Pauline at Mary Malden's home in Mapledale, Berkshires. Loft learns from Reno telegram: Pauline was Hugh Dwyer's wife (married ~8 months, divorced ~6 yrs earlier). Loft tears telegram.
- Ch XIII: Loft plans to falsely confess; suggests Fleming Stone detective.
- Ch XIV: Fleming Stone and Fibsy (Terence McGuire, freckled red-haired Irish lad) arrive. Stone: poison via toothpick? Countess seats Fibsy beside her.
- Ch XV: Stone & Gilvray: puncture in jaw; Stone suspects poison. Fibsy's radio plan (messages "Valentine waiting for Pauline," "Portuguese are the people," "Pearline"); Tessie's clue on New York Central time table, Harlem Division.
- Ch XVI: Pauline's account: Dwyer threatened; she took letters & watch; left at 2 a.m. Hears radio song; phones Loft.
- Ch XVII: Loft drives to Mapledale; Pauline; Loft and Pauline marry at Mapledale (Dr. Messiter); Fibsy buys book at auction (Mr. Baldwin bids winning).
- Ch XVIII: Stone reveals Baldwin's fraud: replaced "Gammer Gurton's Needle" title page with photograph; sold for $20,000; poisoned toothpick; Baldwin swallows poison and dies. Loft and Pauline leave for honeymoon.

**Concluding note:** Baldwin = killer; Pauline innocent; Stone and Fibsy solved via "feathers left around."
